title: Fourier-mode Mirror transform bank
hypothesis: Shared Fourier base and low-description band coordinates preserve multi-domain spectral operator functions with fewer bytes than independent kernels and beat native shared-band controls.
physical_object: shared Fourier-domain operator base and four mode-band atoms
mirror_coordinate: per-domain coefficients over mode-band atoms plus optional sparse private spectral entries
controls: shared bands plus matched top-k private residual

development.selection_metric: relative solution error overall and k>32 band, actual full bank bytes, residual budget

fresh.reason: no audit if development fails or exact native shared-band alias

storage.authority: actual serialized full operator-bank payload bytes

success_gate: Overall and high-band relative error <=.02, >=25% payload savings vs independent kernels, and improve quality/bytes beyond native PCA/shared-band controls.
failure_gate: Quality/storage miss or exact native shared-band function/payload alias => FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
boundaries: Fourier operators are deliberately band-structured; no trained FNO or physical PDE claim.
No fresh/audit or accelerator runtime claim.
